summary: Surya Kanta was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He completed his D.Phil. at the University of Oxford by 1937, studying under Frederick William Thomas, and served as Reader in Sanskrit at the University of the Punjab (attested 1939).

Suryakumar Bhuyan worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Cotton University, Presidency University, the University of Calcutta, and SOAS University of London (PhD 1936), he served as Principal of Cotton University and Vice Chancellor of Gauhati University (~1957–1960).
Suryanarayana Shukla was an Indologist, linguist, and philosopher. He studied at Rajgopal Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya under Nandakishore Pandey, Ramanujacharya, and Shridatta Pandey.

Susan Andrews is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. She earned her PhD from Columbia University (attested 2013), where her doctoral supervisor was Chün-fang Yü, and studied under Bernard Faure, David Max Moerman, Michael I. Como, Koichi Shinohara, and Phyllis Granoff.

Susan J. Rosenfield is an Indologist who completed her PhD at Harvard University in 2004. Her teachers included Stephanie W. Jamison, George L. Hart, Kausalya Hart, Shaligram Shukla, Saudamani Deshmukh, James W. Benson, and Thomas Burke.
Susan L. Beningson works in sinology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Columbia University (attested 2009) under the supervision of Robert E. Harrist, Jr.
Susan L. Huntington is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She was a professor at Ohio State University from approximately 1971 to 2011.
Susan Meinheit is a Tibetologist who held posts at the Library of Congress (attested 1998 and 2007).

Susan Naquin is a historian and sinologist. After earning a BA at Stanford (~1962–1966) and an MA and PhD at Yale (~1966–1974), she taught history at the University of Pennsylvania (1977–1993) and served as professor at Princeton University (1993–2013).

Susan Neiman is a philosopher educated at Harvard (PhD ~1977–1986) and the Free University of Berlin. She held professorships at Yale (1989–1996) and Tel Aviv University (1996–2000), and has served as Director of the Einstein Forum (2000–2026).
Susan Niditch is a religious studies scholar who served as a faculty member in the religion department at Amherst College from approximately 1978 to 2020.

Susan Whitfield is a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and sinology. After completing her PhD at SOAS (1995), she directed the International Dunhuang Project at the British Library (1993–2017) and became Professor at the University of East Anglia.

Susanne Hoeber Rudolph studied at Sarah Lawrence, Harvard (MA, PhD), and Radcliffe. After teaching political science at Harvard (~1955–1963), she was a professor at the University of Chicago (from 1964) and president of the American Political Science Association (2003–2004).

Susanne Mrozik is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who earned an M.T.S. at Harvard, where Charles Hallisey was her doctoral supervisor. She held academic posts at Western Michigan University (attested 2002) and Mount Holyoke College (attested 2009).

Sushanta Sen worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. Educated at Visva-Bharati University, he served there as a lecturer in 1986 and was also Lecturer in Indian Religions in the Department of Theology at the University of Birmingham.

Sushil Kumar De was an Indologist educated at Presidency University, University of Calcutta, SOAS (D.Litt. ~1919–1921), and Bonn. His appointments included positions at the University of Calcutta, Presidency University, University of Dhaka (~1923–1947), and Jadavpur University (1947).
Susmita Basu Majumdar is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Lady Brabourne College and the University of Calcutta, and later held a post at the University of Calcutta.

Susumu Kajiura is a specialist in sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He held a post as an assistant at Kyoto University in 1999 and was head of humanities research at the Gangoji Institute for Research on Cultural Property (attested 2001).

Susumu Otake is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who studied at the University of Tsukuba (~1993–2001) under Makio Takemura. He has held lecturer appointments at Kyoto University (attested 2008), Hanazono University (attested 2008–2013), and Bukkyo University (attested 2012–2013).

Susumu Shimazono is a religious studies and Japanology scholar educated at the University of Tokyo and UC Berkeley. He served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Tokyo (1995–2013) and later held professorial posts at Sophia University.
